methods-and-responsibility.label: Methods and Responsibility
methods-and-responsibility.summary: Put behavior beside the object state it uses, return useful results from model methods, and keep application-wide coordination outside the model.

mc-methods-and-responsibility-class-jobs.title: Which behavior belongs on Car?
mc-methods-and-responsibility-class-jobs.prompt: Which behaviors naturally belong as instance methods on one `Car` object? Choose all that apply.
mc-methods-and-responsibility-class-jobs.hint: Choose behavior that reads or changes one car's own state.

help.concept: An instance method is a good fit when the behavior belongs to one object's state.
help.hint_1: Think about mileage and one-car summaries.
help.hint_2: Fleet-wide reports and user menus coordinate more than one object or the whole application.

options.a: Increase this car's mileage after it drives.
options.b: Return a summary of this car's make, model, and mileage.
options.c: Build a report across every car in the fleet.
options.d: Ask the user which menu option to choose.

sc-methods-and-responsibility-main-role.title: Keep display outside the model
sc-methods-and-responsibility-main-role.prompt: Which design keeps `Car.summary()` focused on the model's responsibility?
sc-methods-and-responsibility-main-role.hint: The method should provide the result; the caller can decide how to display it.

help.concept: Returning a result keeps a model method reusable while `main.py` owns user-facing coordination.
help.hint_1: Avoid putting the application's printing policy inside the model.
help.hint_2: Choose the option where `summary()` returns and `main.py` prints.

options.a: `summary()` prints the text itself and returns nothing.
options.b: `summary()` returns the text, and `main.py` prints the returned value.
options.c: `main.py` rewrites the Car's attributes before every summary.
options.d: `summary()` asks the user which car to summarize.

sketch-0.title: Instance methods own one object's behavior
sketch-0.bodyMarkdown:
An instance method can own a state change that belongs to one object.

```python
class Thermostat:
    def warm_by(self, degrees):
        self.temperature += degrees
        return self.temperature
```

The caller does not need to know how the Thermostat stores or updates its temperature. It asks the object to perform the behavior.

Methods are most useful when the behavior naturally belongs to the object's state.

sketch-1.title: Keep model behavior separate from coordination
sketch-1.bodyMarkdown:
A model method can return useful data while the application decides how to display it.

```python
class Invoice:
    def total(self):
        return self.subtotal + self.tax

invoice = Invoice()
invoice.subtotal = 40
invoice.tax = 3

print(invoice.total())
```

`Invoice.total()` owns the invoice calculation. The outer program owns presentation such as `print()`.

That separation keeps model behavior reusable in a terminal program, web page, test, or report.
